messages:
alex: heads up — we started getting escalations from a customer in eu-west about higher tail latency after the runtime rollout this morning (rollout/2026-03-15-v3.2). p95 jumped and p99 spikes are visible in dashboards :rotating_light:

maria: saw that — started a quick canary check earlier. canary hosts in eu-west-1 saw p95 ~420ms (baseline was ~120ms) and p99 ~1.2s. host-level CPU and GPU util look normal.

sam: deploy-bot shows the canary went out at 08:03 UTC: `deploy-bot: rollout started rollout/2026-03-15-v3.2 -> 5% canary`. Can confirm.

jordan: any error rates or retry storms? support-bot forwarded several 502s from the customer but not widespread. most requests succeed but slower.

alex: stack traces are just slow inference, no OOMs. tracing shows longer kernel selection time and increased KV cache miss rates for some sequences.

maria: I ran a synthetic against the canary with same payloads (multisentence prompts that are ~1k tokens total). here's the curl I used:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b-q4f16","input":"<long prompt>"}'
```

maria: baseline runtime (v3.1) p99: 480ms, v3.2 canary p99: 1.18s for the same batch of 50 concurrent single-shot requests. p95 delta ~+300ms.

sam: interesting: we changed the kernel selection heuristic for short-vs-long sequences in v3.2 to prefer a newer kernel that reduces jitter for small sequences but might add overhead for >512 tokens. could explain high tail for that workload.

jordan: can we reproduce locally with a single model on the same hw? which model? rwd-3b-q4f16 yes.

alex: repro steps I used on a canary node:

1) pull rollout image tag: `registry.redwood/realtime:v3.2-20260315-8f7a`
2) start locally with `--max-seq=1024 --kv-cache=shared`
3) run ab-style concurrent requests (50 concurrency) to /generate with long prompt

I attached the short trace IDs: trace/20260315-az1:ids [trc-33f, trc-40a, trc-4be] showing large kernel select latencies (~120ms per request in select path).

maria: quick mitigation suggestion: rollback canary to v3.1 for eu regions while we bisect. we can also force the older kernel selection via env override `RUNTIME_KERNEL_HEUR=legacy` as a temporary toggle.

oncall-sre: agreed can we do a scoped rollback for canary and reduce traffic to 0% before full rollback? i'll coordinate. :thumbsup:

sam: for bisecting I'll build two intermediate images: one with kernel heuristics flag off (revert) and one with only micro-optimizations from v3.2. we should run an A/B with same synthetic load.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered by oncall-sre: `rollback rollout/2026-03-15-v3.2 -> v3.1` at 08:28 UTC. :white_check_mark:

maria: after rollback p95/p99 in eu-west dropped back near baseline within 3 minutes. customer confirmed latency improved.

alex: capturing artifacts for postmortem:
- k6/gatling synthetic job outputs (canary vs baseline)
- perf flamegraphs for kernel selection path
- trace ids and kv cache stats

jordan: curious why KV cache misses went up — maybe kernel causes different batching window or affects cache key canonicalization. adding kernel to cache-key matrix for repro.

sam: timeline for bisect: I'll cut an image `v3.2-kernel-legacy` and `v3.2-kernel-new` and run a 1-hour canary A/B at 10% each in staging and eu-west. will post results.

maria: tests to run in the bisect: small seqs (<=128), medium (129-512), long (513-1024) and mixed concurrent bursts. capture p50/p95/p99 and kernel-select time.

oncall-sre: also add a traffic shaping test with the customer's real prompt set (we have an anonymized sample from support).

alex: tentative root cause hypothesis: the new kernel heuristics add an extra synchronous check on sequence-length distribution which is cheap for short queries but adds ~100ms overhead on path for long sequences and changes batching expiry, increasing KV cache misses.

sam: if confirmed, next steps: revert heuristic in v3.2 patch (hotfix), add a feature flag gating kernel selection, and extend canary duration with long-sequence synthetic load.

maria: created a ticket PM-4887 to track follow-ups and PRs. assigned sam for bisect/built images, alex for tracing/diagnostics, jordan for cache-key matrix tests.

support-bot: customer update sent at 08:45 UTC: "Thanks — we see latency back to normal after rollback. Please keep us posted on root cause."

alex: quick note for runbook: add a step to include long sequence synthetic workloads in fast canary checklist. missed that in today's canary matrix.

jordan: also add alert rule: if p99 increases by >200% for >5 minutes in canary region, auto-scale down new rollout to 0% and notify oncall.

maria: posting a short log snippet from a canary node showing kernel-sel timings:

```
[2026-03-15T08:14:12Z] kernel_select: model=rwd-3b-q4f16 seq_len=768 select_time_ms=118
[2026-03-15T08:14:12Z] kv_cache: miss=true key=sha256:... lookup_time_ms=7
[2026-03-15T08:14:13Z] exec_start lat_ms=1023
```

sam: collecting perf traces now. will attach flamegraphs to PM-4887.

alex: thanks everyone — good triage. timeline/summary will go into postmortem once bisect completes.

maria: follow-ups: set up the A/B canary for 10:00 UTC, I'll coordinate with oncall and support to keep the customer informed. :eyes:

jordan: closing loop here once bisect results in next 6-8 hours. if hotfix ready earlier we can patch canary then roll forward slowly.

support-bot: incident note created: INC-20260315-1122 (latency regression on rollout v3.2)

alex: end of thread — leaving logs and checklists in PM-4887 and canary-runbook updates in infra repo. :hammer_and_wrench:
